tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a task suggestion you queued earlier with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion has gone stale: the issue was fixed in this session (by you or the user), it turned out not to be a problem after all, or you have queued a better-scoped replacement — in that case queue the replacement with spawn_task first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started or dismissed it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started or dismissed it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

reason.description: Optional short note on why the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34". It doesn't change the outcome.

task_id.description: The task_id from the spawn_task result that queued the suggestion (of the form task_1a2b3c4d).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Suggest a separate task for something you noticed that is outside the scope of your current work.

Call this when you come across something that deserves fixing but doesn't belong in this change — dead code, stale docs, a missing test, a confirmed TODO, a bug or security issue spotted in passing. Don't use it for trivial fixes you can make inline, for anything the user asked you to do, for vague code-smell impressions or unverified hunches, or to split off parts of your own task. The call only queues a suggestion and returns; carry on with your current work.

The user sees a "Suggested task" card in the Claude desktop app with your title and tldr, can open the full prompt, and with one click starts it as a new session — on their machine in their local clone of this repository (optionally a fresh worktree of it), or in the cloud — sends it to this session, or dismisses it. A new session starts from your prompt alone, on a checkout that may not have this session's changes, so the prompt has to stand alone: what to change and why, the files involved by repository-relative path, and any context from this conversation it depends on. Absolute paths and other state of this environment may not exist there. If the find involves a secret or credential, say where it is rather than copying the value, since the prompt is stored and displayed.

The result carries a task_id; if the suggestion later becomes moot, withdraw it with dismiss_task.

prompt.description: The opening message of the new session: the goal, the files involved by repository-relative path, the context it needs from this conversation, and what done looks like. The user can read it in full before starting; markdown is fine. Keep it to what the task needs (hard limit 32000 characters) — the new session can read the code itself.

title.description: The card's heading and the new session's title: a short imperative phrase starting with a verb, under 60 characters, that makes sense on its own — e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option".

tldr.description: One or two plain sentences on what the task would do and why it is worth doing. Shown on the card under the title; it is what the user reads when deciding whether to start it, so no file paths or code.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__add_repo
tools.description:
Add a GitHub repository to the current session so you can read, clone, or operate on it alongside the repos already in the session. Call this whenever you need a repository the session does not have — including when someone only asks a question about one, rather than asking for it to be attached. Prefer attaching a repository over reporting that you cannot reach it. 

IMPORTANT — DO NOT PRE-CHECK THE REPO BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL. Do not curl github.com, do not run `gh repo view`, do not run `git ls-remote` to verify the repo exists. Unauthenticated requests to private repos return 404 ("Not Found") even when the repo is real and your session has authorized access to it. Those preemptive 404s will mislead you into skipping the tool. Instead: call add_repo with the owner/repo exactly as you have it. The backend performs the real reachability + authorization check and returns a structured error you can act on. If the repo genuinely doesn't exist or isn't accessible, the tool response will tell you — report that to the user. If it does exist, the tool response will include a clone command you can then run. Do not report success until the tool has actually been called and returned. 

WHEN ACCESS IS DENIED: if the tool returns an authorization or policy error — the repo exists but isn't enabled for this workspace/project/organization, or the GitHub App isn't installed or linked — relay the tool's exact reason to the user. The response names the remedy: if Claude doesn't have GitHub access for this organization at all, the user should reconnect GitHub under claude.ai Settings → Connectors; if the repo is simply not in the allowed set, a Claude.ai organization owner can grant access in the settings page the response points to. Do not add settings URLs beyond those provided here or in the tool response. Do not retry the same repo. You may remind the user which repositories are already available in this session, and offer to help them request access. Do not guess, infer, or list repositories you cannot see in the tool res… [truncated]

access.description: What access this session needs. "read" (default): fetch/clone only — when the repository is public, git read access is often already served by the session's git proxy with nothing to attach, and the tool says so instead of attaching. "push": the session must push commits, open PRs, or use GitHub API tools against the repository, so it is attached with credentials after the full repository-access checks.

owner.description: GitHub owner (user or organization) of the repo to add, e.g. "anthropics".

repo.description: GitHub repo name, e.g. "claude-code". Do not include the owner prefix — pass owner and repo as separate fields.

tools.description: Archive a Claude Code Remote session. Transitions the session to read-only archived state and releases its container. Use this when a child session has finished its work or is stuck (PR merged, task complete, session failed to initialize) and a human has already acknowledged they're done with the session.

session_id.description: The target session ID to archive.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session
tools.description: Create a new Claude Code Remote session. Returns the new session's ID and status. If environment_id is omitted, the new session inherits the calling session's environment. Combine with send_message for fan-out orchestration: spawn a sibling and send it a task. Where enabled, this session receives a <child-session-event> turn if the new session's turn fails or its worker restarts and drops background tasks; a session that finishes cleanly does not report back, so check on it with get_session (status_bucket reads 'failed' for a turn that errored, where status alone reads 'idle' either way) and list_events.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_session
schema.description: Create a new Claude Code Remote session. Returns the new session's ID and status. If environment_id is omitted, the new session inherits the calling session's environment. Combine with send_message for fan-out orchestration: spawn a sibling and send it a task. Where enabled, this session receives a <child-session-event> turn if the new session's turn fails or its worker restarts and drops background tasks; a session that finishes cleanly does not report back, so check on it with get_session (status_bucket reads 'failed' for a turn that errored, where status alone reads 'idle' either way) and list_events.

append_system_prompt.description: Text appended to the new session's system prompt.

blob_limit_kb.description: Optional. Files larger than this many KB are left out of the checkout; git fetches one on demand when a command reads it. Requires source_url. Set it for very large repositories, whose sessions otherwise fail to start for lack of disk space. Ignored when sparse_checkout_paths is set.

clone_depth.description: Optional number of commits of history to fetch (default 50). Requires source_url. Lower it for very large repositories.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids. When this resolves to the remote_cowork environment (explicitly or via inheritance), a Claude Cowork session is spawned — the account's enabled skills, plugins and the Cowork system prompt are assembled server-side, and only prompt, title, model and tags are read (source_url, extra_allowed_tools, append_system_prompt and environment_variables are ignored so the caller cannot widen the tool surface).

extra_allowed_tools.description: Extra tool names pre-approved without a user permission prompt. Entries the calling session does not itself have pre-approved are dropped — the child never carries a grant its parent lacks.

model.description: Model ID for the new session. Defaults to the calling session's model.

outcome_branch.description: Optional branch name to push changes to. When set, the session pushes directly to this branch (no session-derived suffix appended).

permission_mode.description: Initial permission mode for the new session. Cannot be more permissive than the calling session's mode; omit to inherit it. 'plan' makes the agent propose a plan and then BLOCKS waiting for human approval via the claude.ai/code web UI — do NOT use 'plan' for autonomous child sessions that no human is watching, as they will stall indefinitely at the approval prompt.

prompt.description: Optional initial message to send to the new session.

source_revision.description: Optional git branch, tag, or commit to check out. Requires source_url. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

source_url.description: Optional git repository URL to check out.

sparse_checkout_paths.description: Optional directories, relative to the repository root. The checkout holds only these, plus the files directly in their parent folders and at the root. Requires source_url. Set it to work in part of a very large repository.

tags.description: Free-form tags to categorize the session (e.g. ["remote-agents-project:frontend"]). Editable later via set_session_tags.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
tools.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger
schema.description: Create a Routine (scheduled trigger). Three targeting modes: (1) default — fires into THIS SESSION, resuming the same conversation each time; (2) persistent_session_id set — fires into a SPECIFIC OTHER SESSION you name (must be in your account); (3) create_new_session_on_fire=true — spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing. Use mode 1 for recurring work you want to pick back up yourself; mode 2 for waking a sibling session you created; mode 3 when each firing should start from a clean slate. If the result warns that the Routine stores no connectors, say so plainly when you confirm the Routine to the user and pass on the remedy it names; never report such a Routine as simply created.

connectors.description: Optional list of connector names the Routine's fired sessions may use, e.g. ["Gmail", "linear"]. Pass ONLY connectors the user explicitly asked this Routine to use — the stored grant applies to every future firing. Names resolve against the user's connected claude.ai connectors; when calling from inside a CCR session the list is further limited to connectors that session itself holds (it can only narrow that set, never widen it). Any name that cannot be resolved fails the call. Pass [] to store no connectors. Omit to keep the default behavior for this surface. The grant attaches the connectors only — individual tool calls from fired sessions still go through runtime permission checks.

create_new_session_on_fire.description: If true, each firing creates a fresh session in the calling session's environment instead of resuming an existing one. Default false. Mutually exclusive with persistent_session_id.

cron_expression.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Fields without a prefix are UTC. If you know the user's time zone, write the fields in their local time after CRON_TZ=<IANA time zone> and a space (weekdays at 8:52am in Los Angeles: CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 52 8 * * 1-5). If not, ask. Minimum interval is normally hourly (some projects allow shorter); a too-frequent schedule is rejected and the error names the minimum. For hourly or every-N-hours schedules, use minute 0 (e.g. '0 * * * *', '0 */4 * * *'): the server anchors it to the creation minute ('hourly starting now'), so Routines spread across the hour instead of all firing at :00. All other schedules are stored verbatim. When a recurring schedule (run_once_at is unset) at a fixed time of day would land on the hour or half hour (a plain '9am' or '9:30'), prefer using a jittered minute value instead. Most schedules run on minute 0, so runs scheduled at those times can be delayed due to server traffic. By default, move the time 1 to 15 minutes earlier (for '9am', 8:45 to 8:59); use the number of letters in the task's name, modulo 15, plus 1. Leave midnight, a time on any other minute (e.g. 9:10) and a run that must follow an event as asked. Mutually exclusive with run_once_at. Omit both for a poke-only Routine that never fires on its own schedule.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Required when calling from outside a CCR session (no session context to inherit from). Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids.

initiation.description: Who wanted this: human_request — a person asked you to set this up now; human_schedule — a schedule a person set (e.g. an earlier firing) told you to; own_followup — your own check-in or follow-up on work you are already doing; own_initiative — you decided on your own that this should exist.

notifications.description: Completion notifications for this Routine. push sends to the owner's phone when a run finishes with something noteworthy; email sends the same summary to their inbox. If omitted, the setting stays unset and the server default applies at fire time. Passing this sets an explicit per-Routine choice, so list every channel you want on ({push:true, email:true} for both; {email:true} alone means email-only, push off). Pass {} to opt out of all channels. Only fresh-session-per-fire Routines (create_new_session_on_fire=true) take this; the server rejects it for self-bind or persistent_session_id Routines.

persistent_session_id.description: Optional session ID to fire into instead of this one. Must belong to the same account — the server rejects sessions you don't own. Omit to fire into this session (default). Mutually exclusive with create_new_session_on_fire.

prompt.description: The message the Routine sends on each firing. When binding to an existing session (modes 1-2), write it assuming past context — the conversation continues. In fresh-session mode (mode 3), write it as a complete standalone instruction since each firing starts from nothing.

run_once_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp for a one-shot fire (e.g. 2026-04-20T17:00:00Z). Must be in the future. Mutually exclusive with cron_expression — set one or the other, not both. After the one-shot fires the Routine disables itself with ended_reason=run_once_fired. Use exactly the time asked: the guidance on recurring schedules does not apply to a one-time run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__delete_trigger
tools.description: Delete a Routine (scheduled trigger). The Routine must belong to the calling session's account — deleting another account's Routine fails with not-found. Use this to undo a create_trigger call or to clean up Routines whose work is done. A bad cron or wrong prompt does not need deletion — update_trigger fixes those in place, keeping the Routine's run history. On success, the result usually echoes the deleted Routine's last state (including its name) in the response's trigger field — callers without stored-data read access get a plain-text confirmation instead. Either way the Routine no longer exists once this returns.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__get_session
tools.description: Get details for a specific Claude Code Remote session by ID. Returns the session's title, status, status_bucket (working / blocked / review_ready / completed / failed — 'failed' means its last turn errored), creation time, and context. Every returned session carries three model fields: configured_model is the model stored at creation, echoed as stored (it may be an alias or carry a context-window suffix, so normalize before comparing); session_context.model is the model the session is currently set to run (the creation-time model, or a later switch or refusal fallback); external_metadata.last_served_model is the model the CLI ran the latest turn on, which also reflects turn-scoped fallbacks (overload or unavailable) that do not change session_context.model. To detect a switch or fallback in a child session, compare configured_model against both session_context.model and external_metadata.last_served_model; the fallback notices in list_events give the reason. Omit session_id to describe this session.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__list_triggers
tools.description: List Routines (scheduled triggers) owned by this account. Use it to find trigger IDs (trig_...) for update_trigger and delete_trigger. From a thread in a Slack channel, only Routines that fire into that thread's session are listed unless all_in_channel is true. Each entry has the Routine's id, name, cron_expression, run_once_at, enabled state, ended_reason, next_run_at, created_at, persistent_session_id, and last_run. last_run is the most recent recorded run {status, fired_at, finished_at, session_id}. It is absent when no run was recorded (e.g. never fired). For a Routine that wakes an existing session, last_run records that the wake was delivered (SUCCEEDED) or failed to deliver, not how the turn went, unless run tracking covers that session. A FAILED or repeatedly non-SUCCEEDED last_run means the Routine is not doing its job. ended_reason says why a disabled Routine is permanently disabled. suspension_reason (e.g. subscription_paused) marks a temporary hold that lifts when the owner's subscription resumes. Both empty means user-paused. One-shot Routines that already fired (e.g. delivered send_later reminders) and Routines moved to a project are hidden unless include_completed is true. Scheduled tasks stored locally by the Cowork desktop app are not listed.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__read_documentation
tools.description: The documentation for the machine and product this session runs in: a claude.ai cloud container and the settings around it (GitHub access, connectors, the environment's secrets, network access, setup script and installed tools, the session's limits, Remote Control). Read it whenever something about your container or environment comes up, whether it blocked you, you worked around it, or the person asked how to set it up. For example: the repository the work is about is not in your container, a clone or push is refused, a service you need has no connected connector, an outbound host is denied, a command-line tool is missing, you need an API key. Read it rather than answering from memory because these settings move and get renamed faster than your training data, and a page says what is true now: the current steps, where in the product the person makes the change, and what you can do yourself. Reading a page also helps the person directly: in the Claude Code app they see a card with a button that takes them to that settings page, so they can fix it themselves while you carry on. Call it with no topic to list the pages and when each applies; call it with a topic to read that page. Read a page each time a different topic comes up; one read per topic is enough. It is read-only and needs no approval. It has nothing on bugs in the code you are working on.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

1	"""operating_point_sizing, step 1: the OPERATING POINT of the gate_family finalists (DESIGN_PANEL quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip
2	merged with decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control; Judge 2's merge, both judges' caveats binding). IS only.
3	
4	THIS STEP ADDS NO OOS CANDIDATE. It re-parameterises the gate_family sub-family finalists' OOF scores (a threshold on a score
5	another study produced is not a gate: Judge 1); gate_family itself wrote NO candidate (null on both timeframes), so every kept
6	book here is a re-parameterisation of a gate that already failed harness.go_no_go. Every threshold evaluated for a kept-vs-skipped
7	number is a harness.score row (family operating_point/<sub>); the kept-vs-skipped numbers below come from those rows only.
8	
9	Inputs   studies/gate_family/results/oof_<tf>.parquet: the 12-block purged OOF probability p (column `p`) of every probability
10	         learner of the two sub-families ((I) context: hour_bin one-hot + dir, inside the frozen vocabulary; (II) h5_full: the
11	         full as-of table, OUTSIDE THE FROZEN SHORTLIST (importance rule failed for every cluster)). Scored models = the
12	         deployable scorecard of each sub-family (Platt-mapped integer score -> p, per fold) and the HGB classifier (the
13	         gradient-boosting ceiling / the (I) finalist on minute). The policy trees (pt1-3, the 5minute (I) finalist pt2) and the
14	         H5 rule list carry no score: they cannot be thresholded and are not here (stated in FINDINGS).
15	Score    s = 1 - p (nonconformity of the label 'win'). Everything is a threshold on s; keep iff s <= threshold.
16	Labels   L1 (harness.load(tf)); folds = harness blocks (the OOF parquet's `fold` equals T.block on every IS row, asserted).
17	
18	(1) Cross-conformal, Mondrian by class (winner coverage): for fold f, calibration = the OOF scores of the TRUE WINNERS of the
19	    other 11 folds; q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest; the prediction set of a fold-f row contains 'win' iff
20	    s <= q_alpha; skip iff 'win' is not in the set. alpha in {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}. Reported per fold: nominal alpha vs
21	    empirical OOF winner coverage (count and |net|-weighted), kept share; pooled: the ledger row (controls on). CV+ caveat (Judge
22	    2): the calibration scores come from models that saw fold f, so the finite-sample guarantee is the weaker cross-conformal /
23	    CV+ form (about 1 - 2 alpha), not 1 - alpha; both are printed next to the empirical coverage.
24	    Time-bin taxonomy (class x bin; minute only, Judge 2): bins 09:15-10:29 / 10:30-12:59 / 13:00-15:19 by the SETUP bar's clock
25	    (`time`; the bins do not align with hour_bin's edges, so the taxonomy reads the clock, an identity column - a deployable
26	    form would need a clock key); calibration winners and q_alpha per bin.
27	    ACI (Gibbs & Candes 2021), winner-conditional: rows in time order; alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t) updated at
28	    every TRUE WINNER row (err_t = 1 when that winner was skipped), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}; the quantile at row t is the
29	    Mondrian quantile at level alpha_t over the OOF scores of the winners seen BEFORE t (expanding window; first ACI_BURN_IN
30	    winners: keep everything, counted); alpha_t clipped to [0, 1] (alpha_t <= 0 keeps everything, >= 1 skips everything).
31	    Its final state (alpha_T, q_T, n winners) is what oos_once would carry forward; no OOS row is read.
32	(2) Selective risk-coverage curve: coverage c in {0.10, 0.15, ..., 1.00}; nested: the fold-f threshold is the c-quantile of s over
33	    the other 11 folds' rows; selective risk = mean of min(max(-net, 0), 6000) among kept; the loser share among kept; the
34	    realised coverage. Every c is a ledger row (controls off: trials).
35	(3) Conformal Risk Control (Angelopoulos, Bates, Candes, Jordan & Lei 2022) with SESSIONS as units: calibration block = the last
36	    200 IS sessions with a SETUP (n stated as sessions-with-SETUPs; the OOF scores of its rows come from the purged folds, so the
37	    block is not disjoint in time from every score's training folds - the CV+ caveat again, stated); for coverage lambda on the
38	    grid the threshold is the lambda-quantile of s over the block's rows; per session r_s(lambda) = mean clipped loss of the
39	    session's kept units (0 when none kept: no trade, no loss); R_hat = mean over the n sessions; certificate =
40	    (n R_hat + B) / (n + 1), B = 6000; lambda* = the largest lambda with certificate <= alpha, alpha in {800, 1000, 1200} INR
41	    (the cost level); the gate s <= threshold(lambda*) on all IS is a ledger row (controls on); the realised risk on the IS rows
42	    before the block is reported beside the certificate. Per-bin certificates on minute only (dropped on 5m: Judge 2).
43	(4) Cost-aware Pareto front: for every coverage-curve row U_w = kept net - w x sum over skipped of max(net, 0), w in {0, 0.5, 1};
44	    winner-net retained = kept winners' net / all winners' net (the row's winner_recall_weighted); loser-net avoided = skipped
45	    losers' |net| / all losers' |net|; the non-dominated points are flagged; the argmax per w is printed for the user to pick
46	    (Rule 0(c)). Nothing is chosen here.
47	(5) Cost sensitivity of every kept book: kept mean at 3 / 5 / 8 pts slippage per side (the ledger row's kept_mean_slip3 /
48	    kept_mean / kept_mean_slip8) and with the brokerage cap of 20 INR per order replaced by uncapped 0.03% (lab.trade_charges with
49	    brokerage_cap = inf, slippage 5); the harness item is kept_mean_slip8 > 0.
50	
51	Family: operating_point/<conformal | conformal_timebin | aci | coverage | crc | crc_timebin>; PBO (diff), SPA, effective trials,
52	DSR over every operating_point row of the timeframe; harness.go_no_go on the best row with null_tape = 'not run: this step adds no
53	candidate' (fails by design) and the model's source columns declared.
54	"""
55	import os, sys, json, math, time, argparse, datetime as D
56	sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
57	import numpy as np, pandas as pd
58	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
59	OUT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
60	if OUT not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, OUT)
61	import harness as H                                                     # noqa: E402
62	import lab                                                              # noqa: E402  trade_charges only (via harness.LAB path)
63	
64	ALPHAS = [0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30]
65	GAMMAS = [0.005, 0.01]
66	ACI_BURN_IN = 30
67	COVERAGES = [round(0.10 + 0.05 * i, 2) for i in range(19)]             # 0.10 .. 1.00
68	CRC_LAMBDAS = [round(0.05 * i, 2) for i in range(1, 21)]                # 0.05 .. 1.00
69	CRC_ALPHAS = [800.0, 1000.0, 1200.0]
70	CRC_SESSIONS = 200
71	CLIP_B = 6000.0
72	W_GRID = [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]
73	BINS = [("09:15-10:29", 0, 630), ("10:30-12:59", 630, 780), ("13:00-15:19", 780, 10 ** 6)]
74	MODELS = [("context", "hgbc"), ("context", "scorecard"), ("h5_full", "hgbc"), ("h5_full", "scorecard")]
75	VOCAB = {"context": "inside the frozen vocabulary (context columns)",
76	         "h5_full": "outside the frozen shortlist (importance rule failed for every cluster)"}
77	ROLE = {("minute", "context", "hgbc"): "finalist of sub-family (I) (hgbc -> distilled tree; this is the hgbc OOF p)",
78	        ("minute", "context", "scorecard"): "the deployable scorecard of sub-family (I)",
79	        ("minute", "h5_full", "scorecard"): "finalist of sub-family (II) (scorecard -> distilled tree; this is the scorecard OOF p)",
80	        ("minute", "h5_full", "hgbc"): "gradient-boosting ceiling of sub-family (II) (reference)",
81	        ("5minute", "context", "hgbc"): "probability learner of sub-family (I) (its finalist pt2 is a policy tree with no score)",
82	        ("5minute", "context", "scorecard"): "the deployable scorecard of sub-family (I)",
83	        ("5minute", "h5_full", "scorecard"): "finalist of sub-family (II) (scorecard -> distilled rules; this is the scorecard OOF p)",
84	        ("5minute", "h5_full", "hgbc"): "gradient-boosting ceiling of sub-family (II) (reference)"}
85	GF_RES = os.path.join(OUT, "studies", "gate_family", "results")
86	
87	
88	def log(*a):
89	    print(D.datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S"), *a, flush=True)
90	
91	
92	def r2(x): return None if x is None or (isinstance(x, float) and not np.isfinite(x)) else round(float(x), 2)
93	def r4(x): return None if x is None or (isinstance(x, float) and not np.isfinite(x)) else round(float(x), 4)
94	
95	
96	def source_columns(tf, sub):
97	    cols = json.load(open(os.path.join(GF_RES, tf, sub, "features.json")))["cols"]
98	    src = sorted({c.split("=")[0].replace("__na", "") for c in cols})
99	    return src
100	
101	
102	def mondrian_q(cal, alpha):
103	    """The ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest calibration score; +inf when the rank exceeds n (keep everything)."""
104	    cal = np.sort(np.asarray(cal, dtype=float)); n = len(cal)
105	    if n == 0: return math.inf
106	    k = int(math.ceil((n + 1) * (1 - alpha)))
107	    return math.inf if k > n else (float(cal[k - 1]) if k >= 1 else -math.inf)
108	
109	
110	def clipped_loss(net): return np.minimum(np.maximum(-net, 0.0), CLIP_B)
111	
112	
113	def uncapped_net(T):
114	    """Every unit's net at 5 pts slippage with the brokerage cap removed (0.03% per order uncapped); lab.trade_charges."""
115	    cs = dict(H.CS); cs["brokerage_cap"] = float("inf")
116	    out = np.empty(T.n)
117	    for i in range(T.n):
118	        e, x = T.entry_px[i], T.exit_px[i]
119	        if T.up[i]: buy, sell = e + H.SLIP, x - H.SLIP
120	        else: sell, buy = e - H.SLIP, x + H.SLIP
121	        out[i] = (sell - buy) * H.LOT - lab.trade_charges(cs, buy, sell, H.LOT)["total"]
122	    return out
123	
124	
125	def book_stats(T, keep, rows, net_unc):
126	    """Kept-only / skipped-only statistics that are NOT kept-vs-skipped differences (those come from the ledger row)."""
127	    k = rows[keep[rows]]; s = rows[~keep[rows]]; net = T.net
128	    W = T.win[rows]; wn = net[rows]
129	    win_net = wn[W].sum(); loss_net = -wn[~W].sum()
130	    out = dict(selective_risk=r2(clipped_loss(net[k]).mean()) if len(k) else None,
131	               loser_share_kept=r4((~T.win[k]).mean()) if len(k) else None,
132	               skipped_winner_net=r2(net[s][net[s] > 0].sum()) if len(s) else 0.0,
133	               winner_net_retained=r4(net[k][net[k] > 0].sum() / win_net) if win_net else None,
134	               loser_net_avoided=r4(-net[s][net[s] <= 0].sum() / loss_net) if loss_net else None,
135	               kept_mean_uncapped=r2(net_unc[k].mean()) if len(k) else None,
136	               skipped_mean_uncapped=r2(net_unc[s].mean()) if len(s) else None)
137	    for w in W_GRID: out[f"U_w{w}"] = r2(net[k].sum() - w * (net[s][net[s] > 0].sum() if len(s) else 0.0))
138	    return out
139	
140	
141	def pick(res):
142	    keys = ("id", "kept_n", "kept_share", "kept_mean", "skipped_mean", "diff", "diff_top1_removed", "kept_mean_slip3", "kept_mean_slip8",
143	            "loser_recall", "loser_precision", "winner_recall", "winner_recall_weighted", "top_decile_winners_skipped", "sign_blocks",
144	            "perm_p", "control_pct", "kept_net", "skipped_net", "kept_win_rate", "kept_pf")
145	    return {k: res.get(k) for k in keys}
146	
147	
148	def run(tf):
149	    t0 = time.time()
150	    T = H.load(tf)
151	    is_idx = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
152	    order = is_idx[np.argsort(T.setup_i[is_idx], kind="stable")]              # IS rows in time order
153	    oof = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(GF_RES, f"oof_{tf}.parquet"))
154	    hm = pd.to_datetime(T.F.time.astype(str)).dt.hour.to_numpy() * 60 + pd.to_datetime(T.F.time.astype(str)).dt.minute.to_numpy()
155	    tbin = np.array([next(name for name, lo, hi in BINS if lo <= m < hi) for m in hm])
156	    net_unc = uncapped_net(T)
157	    act = T.active_sessions; cal_sessions = set(int(s) for s in act[-CRC_SESSIONS:])
158	    cal_rows = is_idx[np.isin(T.session[is_idx], list(cal_sessions))]
159	    pre_rows = is_idx[~np.isin(T.session[is_idx], list(cal_sessions))]
160	    log(f"{tf}: {T.n} units, IS {len(is_idx)}, active IS sessions {len(act)}, CRC block = last {CRC_SESSIONS} active sessions -> {len(cal_rows)} rows "
161	        f"(from session {act[-CRC_SESSIONS]}, {T.day[cal_rows].min()} .. {T.day[cal_rows].max()}); rows before the block {len(pre_rows)}")
162	    meta = dict(tf=tf, label="L1", is_units=int(len(is_idx)), all_mean=r2(T.net[is_idx].mean()), win_rate=r4(T.win[is_idx].mean()),
163	                winners=int(T.win[is_idx].sum()), active_sessions=int(len(act)), mean_cost=r2(T.F.l1_cost_inr.to_numpy()[is_idx].mean()),

20	
21	1. **Read the tables through `harness.load(tf)`** (label `L1` = the intraday 15:25 book, the training label; `L0` = the engine's
22	   uncut trade, robustness only). Features come from `Table.asof_columns()` / `harness.design(T)`; never a column with prefix
23	   `fnd_`, `l1_`, `fwd_`, `fzpos_`, `fzpost_`, nor `fz_traded`, nor a final-state field of the side tables.
24	2. **IS only.** `harness.score(..., split="IS")` is the only source of a kept-vs-skipped number; it refuses `split="OOS"` unless
25	   the caller is `oos_once.py`. Do not read `split == "OOS"` rows for anything but a row count.
26	3. **Every configuration tried is a ledger row**: call `score()` for every threshold / rule / model variant you evaluate, with
27	   `family="<study>/<sub-family>"` and the exact `config` dict. PBO, DSR and SPA are computed over the family from the ledger.

29	   thresholds inside training folds; report the CPCV path distribution (median, 5th percentile), never one number.
30	5. **Judgement** = kept-vs-skipped expectancy (INR per trade), the session-matched random-control percentile, the permutation p,
31	   loser recall / precision, |net|-weighted winner recall, top-decile winners skipped, the difference with the top 1% winners
32	   removed, the kept book's mean at 8 pts slippage, the block-wise sign count. Net alone is never the criterion.

34	   bins and integer points, or two numbers; provenance = `learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha <ledger row id>`.

Every gate candidate goes through score(); kept-vs-skipped expectancy, session-matched random control (fz_report.random_control), permutation p (fz_report.permutation_p), CPCV 11 paths, go/no-go rule (PBO <= 0.2, CPCV p5 diff > 0, DSR p < 0.1, kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300/80, top-1%-removed value > 0, slippage 8 pts survival). 260	### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)
261	
262	**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.
263	
264	**what_it_answers.** The user's acceptance criterion made formal: can SETUPs be skipped with a finite-sample guarantee that at most alpha of the true winners are skipped (marginally over SETUPs, under exchangeability), what skip rate, loser recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy each alpha buys on IS out-of-fold, whether the winner coverage holds on OOS, what the hour-of-day guarantee costs in sample size, and how far a coverage-chosen threshold sits from the expectancy-chosen threshold of the meta-label study.
265	
266	**method.** Score s(x) = 1 - p_win_hat(x) taken from the meta-label study's IS out-of-fold probabilities (the scorecard variant, since the forest cannot live in the lab; the forest's scores are reported as reference). Cross-conformal / CV+ flavour: no separate calibration split is sacrificed (181 winners on 5m IS cannot afford one); within the harness's 12 purged folds, the conformal quantile is computed on the OOF scores of the winners in 11 folds and applied to the 12th, so the IS evaluation is itself out-of-fold. Mondrian by class: q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest OOF score among true winners; the prediction set contains 'win' iff s(x) <= q_alpha; gate = skip iff 'win' is not in the set, i.e. p_win_hat(x) < 1 - q_alpha. Guarantee: P(win in set | true winner) >= 1 - alpha, so at most alpha of winners are skipped in expectation; nothing is guaranteed for losers, their recall is measured. Alpha grid {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}; the smallest feasible alpha is 1/(n_win + 1) (0.0055 on 5m IS). Time taxonomy: class x time bin with three bins fixed in advance (09:15-10:29, 10:30-12:59, 13:00-15:19; the IS hour profile shows morning losses and afternoon gains); feasibility stated from winner counts per bin (5m IS: 16-39 winners per hour, so per-bin guarantees only for alpha >= 0.1; on 1m roughly 4-5x more). Robustness: |net|-weighted coverage (share of winners' gross net kept) reported next to count coverage, because the guarantee is per SETUP, not per rupee. Evaluation on IS-OOF per alpha: skip rate, winner coverage, loser recall, kept-vs-skipped expectancy and permutation p, control percentile (fz_report.random_control), top-decile-winner coverage; alpha chosen on IS by the pre-registered rule 'largest loser recall subject to winner coverage >= 0.9 and kept-vs-skipped difference > 0'. Exchangeability check: coverage per IS year and against the regime study's break tests. ACI variant (Gibbs and Candes): alpha_t+1 = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}, run sequentially over IS in time order, then continued into OOS from IS's final state without re-tuning, to see whether an online alpha keeps coverage under drift. OOS once: the frozen (alpha, taxonomy, thresholds) and the frozen ACI state, same table.
267	
268	**leakage_controls.** Scores are out-of-fold from the purged, embargoed splitter; the conformal quantile uses only winners from calibration folds; alpha, the time bins and the selection rule are fixed before OOS; ACI's state carries forward without any OOS tuning; the study reads no OOS row until the single frozen run; the comparison with the expectancy-chosen tau is on IS-OOF only.
269	
270	**compute.** Quantiles over <= 5k scores x 5 alphas x 12 folds and a sequential ACI loop over <= 5k rows: under 1 CPU-minute, under 100 MB; it depends only on the meta-label study's OOF file.
271	
272	**libraries.** numpy, pandas; mapie is not installed and not needed (split/cross-conformal quantile and ACI are about 40 lines); fz_report.random_control / permutation_p read-only.
273	
274	**output_as_config.** A "conformal" block in ST13/ST14: {"alpha": 0.10, "taxonomy": "class" or "class_x_timebin", "time_bins": [["09:15","10:29"],["10:30","12:59"],["13:00","15:19"]], "skip_if_score_below": s (per bin, the deployable scorecard's score at 1 - q_alpha), "calibration": {"n_winners": n, "is_window": "2021-10-01..2025-12-31", "oof_scores_sha": ...}, "aci": {"enabled": false or true, "gamma": 0.01, "alpha_state": a}}. The lab compares the scorecard score with a number; nothing else is code. Because the threshold is a single number per bin, it is the most compact form any gate in this study set can take.
275	
276	**novelty.** Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer (2005) Algorithmic Learning in a Random World; Mondrian conformal prediction (Vovk 2012); cross-conformal (Vovk 2015) and CV+ / jackknife+ (Barber, Candes, Ramdas and Tibshirani 2021, Annals of Statistics); Angelopoulos and Bates (2021) A gentle introduction to conformal prediction; Gibbs and Candes (2021) Adaptive Conformal Inference under distribution shift, NeurIPS. Current because conformal sets on top of a meta-labelling model are the 2021-2025 way to turn 'skip only losers' into a coverage statement with a finite-sample guarantee; it is not in AFML but is the natural successor to its bet-sizing chapter.
277	
278	**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: the guarantee is on winner count while P&L sits in the tail (a gate can keep 90% of winners and skip the three that made the year), exchangeability fails across the IS/OOS shift (5m -277 to -1,060), and the threshold it selects is the same number study 2 selects by expectancy, so it changes no trade. Fix: do not run as a study; report |net|-weighted coverage of the frozen gate as one row of study 2's OOS table; if a guarantee is ever wanted, weighted conformal on |net| with sessions as units.
279	
280	**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: State the cross-conformal caveat: the OOF scores of the 11 calibration folds come from models that saw the 12th fold, so the finite-sample guarantee is the weaker CV+ / jackknife+ form (roughly 1 - 2 alpha), not 1 - alpha; report empirical OOF winner coverage per fold next to the nominal alpha. Merge with decision-making-4 into ONE operating-point step that reports both guarantees (winner coverage here, kept-loss risk there) on the same scorecard score, presents the Pareto front, and lets the user pick the point (Rule 0(c)); it is the same candidate as the scorecard for the OOS budget, not a second OOS look. Time-bin taxonomy only on 1m (5m has 16-39 winners per hour). Compute < 1 min.
281	
282	### quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing (priority 5)
283	
284	**technique.** Probability calibration on purged out-of-fold predictions (isotonic and Platt, nested), expected-net sizing under the asymmetric payoff (Kelly fraction with class-conditional mean win and loss) discretised to 0-3 lots, compared with AFML's symmetric z-score sizing, judged with a lot-aware extension of the session-matched random control.
285	
286	**what_it_answers.** Given a calibrated p_win and the asymmetric payoff (5m IS: 22% winners, win mean +10,878 INR, loss mean -3,429 INR, top-decile winners 46% of gross wins), how many lots per SETUP, whether sizing adds expectancy per lot beyond the skip decision, whether the calibration is real (reliability curve, Brier skill against the 22% base rate, ECE) on IS-OOF and once on OOS, and whether the honest answer with 181 winners is simply 'one lot or skip'.
287	
288	**method.** Calibration: sklearn IsotonicRegression (and Platt via LogisticRegression as the low-variance alternative) fitted on the meta-label study's IS OOF p_hat against the L1 label, nested inside the harness splitter (fit on 11 folds' OOF, apply to the 12th); reliability curves in 5 quantile bins, Brier score and Brier skill score versus the base rate, expected calibration error, per model (scorecard is the deployable one). Conditional payoffs: W(x), L(x) = mean net of winners and of losers within calibrated-probability quintiles on the training folds; a HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='quantile' (0.5) on |net| is tried only if the importance study shows any feature predicts magnitude (prior: it does not; say so). Expected net e(x) = p_hat W - (1 - p_hat) L. Sizing rules compared: (a) AFML 10.3 for reference: m = 2 Phi(z) - 1 with z = (p_hat - 0.5) / sqrt(p_hat (1 - p_hat)), which is wrong at a 22% base rate and is shown to be so; (b) Kelly fraction f = p_hat / L_bar - (1 - p_hat) / W_bar, half-Kelly, mapped to lots by fixed bins; (c) expected-net bins: lots = 0 if e(x) < 0, 1 if e(x) < c1, 2 if e(x) < c2, else 3, with (c1, c2) on a coarse grid (multiples of the median cost, about 1,100 INR) chosen inside folds; every (c1, c2) tried goes to the harness ledger. Book: lots x the intraday Foundation net with charges recomputed per lot via lab.trade_charges (brokerage cap per order matters) and slippage per lot. Judgement: net per lot, kept-vs-skipped per lot, maximum drawdown and per-session Sharpe of the sized book versus the 1-lot gated book versus raw Foundation; lot-aware control: extend fz_report.random_control so each draw assigns the study's own multiset of lot sizes per session to randomly chosen Foundation positions of that session (seeded the same way), giving the percentile and p_beat of the sized book; block-bootstrap confidence intervals from the harness. Sample-size statement: two cut points learned on about 180 winners on 5m give wide intervals; if the CPCV 5th percentile of net-per-lot improvement is not above zero, the study's recommendation is 'lots = 1 or skip' and the size block carries that verdict. OOS once with the frozen calibration map and bins.
289	
290	**leakage_controls.** Calibration fitted on OOF predictions only and nested in the same purged, embargoed folds; W_bar, L_bar and the lot cut points from training folds only; no label information in x (as-of allowlist); the calibration map and bins are frozen with a sha before OOS; the lot-aware control uses the same seeding discipline as fz_report so the percentile reproduces; net per lot is the selection statistic so that adding lots to a few large winners cannot masquerade as skill without the control percentile agreeing.
291	
292	**compute.** Isotonic and Platt fits: milliseconds; sizing grid of about 20 (c1, c2) pairs x 12 folds: seconds; lot-aware random control 2,000 draws x 1,026 sessions vectorised in numpy: under 1 minute; peak under 100 MB.
293	
294	**libraries.** sklearn (IsotonicRegression, LogisticRegression, CalibratedClassifierCV with the harness splitter as cv iterable, HistGradientBoostingRegressor), numpy, pandas, scipy.stats.norm; lab.trade_charges and fz_report.random_control read-only.
295	
296	**output_as_config.** A "size" block in ST13/ST14: {"lots_max": 3, "rule": "expected_net_bins", "expected_net_inr_bins": [0, c1, c2], "lots": [0, 1, 2, 3], "payoff_table": {"quintile_edges": [...], "win_mean_inr": [...], "loss_mean_inr": [...]}, "calibration": {"method": "isotonic", "knots": [[score, p], ...] at most 10}} with provenance; the isotonic map is a monotone step function so a knot table is a legitimate config, and the lab's position.lots becomes per-signal (it already prices charges per lot). If the verdict is 'one lot or skip', the block records that with the CPCV numbers that produced it.
297	
298	**novelty.** AFML (2018) ch. 10 (bet sizing from predicted probabilities, sizing discretisation, averaging active bets); Kelly (1956); Zadrozny and Elkan (2002) isotonic calibration; Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana (2005); Guo et al. (2017) expected calibration error; the asymmetric-payoff correction to AFML 10.3 is the standard critique in the meta-labelling follow-ups (Joubert 2022; Meyer, Barziy and Joubert 2023, J. Financial Data Science). Current because calibrated-probability sizing with an explicit payoff table is how a meta-labelling model is turned into position size in 2020s practice, and because the lab already has the lot machinery to consume it.
299	
300	**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 3 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: two lot cut points learned on ~180 winners; the brokerage cap makes multi-lot cheaper per lot, a mechanical 'sizing works' effect; sizing multiplies whatever the gate got wrong on a book whose raw edge is negative. Fix: defer until a gate has passed OOS; then one table only, Platt not isotonic, charges per lot held at the 1-lot rate to remove the cap effect, and the answer is 'one lot or skip' or a 2-step monotone schedule; it never consumes an OOS candidate slot.
301	
302	**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Sizing multiplies an edge that is not yet shown to exist (Kelly at the base rate is negative: 0.22/3429 - 0.78/10878 < 0) and per-signal lots is a lab code change the user has not approved. Fold into one conditional step merged with decision-making-5, run only after a gate passes the harness go/no-go with CPCV 5th-percentile kept expectancy > 0; default verdict 'one lot or skip' with the CPCV numbers. Keep the isotonic reliability curve and Brier skill as a diagnostic inside the meta-label study (seconds). The lot-aware random_control extension must be a scratchpad copy, never an edit of fz_report.

392	### decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control (priority 4)
393	
394	**technique.** Selective classification with a reject option and conformal risk control: a distribution-free finite-sample certificate on the loss of the kept trades, the winner-retained vs loser-avoided Pareto front, and cost-assumption sensitivity, to fix the gate's operating point
395	
396	**what_it_answers.** Where to set the gate's threshold so that it "avoids only loss trades and not profitable ones" in a quantified, certified way: for a chosen coverage (share of SETUPs kept) what mean loss / loser share among kept trades can be guaranteed, how much winner-net is given up, and whether the chosen point survives slippage of 3 / 5 / 8 pts per side.
397

416	**technique.** Position sizing as a Kelly-bounded policy: fractional / risk-constrained Kelly on the calibrated conditional edge, with estimation shrinkage from session-block bootstrap, mapped to a monotone lots-by-edge step function
417	
418	**what_it_answers.** Whether, once a positive-conditional-edge region exists, sizing 1-3 lots by predicted edge improves log-growth and drawdown over flat sizing at the same average lots, and what the bounded, monotone lots schedule is; or, honestly, that the edge is not positive enough anywhere and the answer is 0 lots (the raw book has win rate 15% and mean -922 INR, i.e. negative Kelly).
419	
420	**method.** Inputs: out-of-fold IS predictions from study 1 (E[net|x] plus 0.1/0.5/0.9 quantiles from HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='quantile'), realised net per SETUP, capital C = futures_margin 120,000 x 3 lots + 60,000 buffer (from the strategy files), per-lot charges from lab.trade_charges (brokerage cap makes cost slightly sublinear in lots). Bucket SETUPs by out-of-fold edge decile; per bucket estimate the return-on-capital distribution by stationary session-block bootstrap (2,000 draws) and compute the Kelly fraction f* = argmax E[log(1 + f R)] (scipy scalar optimisation; R = net per lot / C), the risk-constrained variant with a drawdown constraint P(drawdown > 20%) <= 0.1 (Busseti-Ryu-Boyd bound, 1-D per bucket), and the shrunk fraction f_s = 0.5 x the bootstrap 25th percentile of f*. Lots(bucket) = clip(floor(f_s x C / margin_per_lot), 0, 3), then enforced monotone non-decreasing in the edge bucket with <= 3 steps (isotonic step fit). Evaluate by replay with the lab's lock (one open position per contract) and 15:25 square-off on IS CV: terminal log-growth, max drawdown, Sharpe-like t on daily net, vs flat 1-lot, flat 3-lot and a lots-matched flat book (same total lots traded).     return "\n".join(out)
